purpose: Compare advertised consumer promises against total cost and real alternatives without inventing unobserved prices

principles: Regulator allegations are not proven violations
A settlement may not admit liability
Never turn a formula into a dollar total without dated verified inputs
Do not infer deceptive intent from a more expensive plan
Use same horizon, units and service requirements across alternatives
Treat unknown fees and household bundle effects as unknown rather than zero

measurementStatuses.verified-example: Numerical constraints or prices documented in primary terms; not a personal bill
measurementStatuses.formula-only: Cost calculation is specified but required transaction inputs are not established

scenarios.name: T-Mobile / T-Mix

consumerCostModel.headline: Two simultaneous phone discounts
consumerCostModel.advertised: Up to $1,200 off a qualifying phone
consumerCostModel.constraint: Each $1,200 deal uses 3 Picks; a two-line T-Mix More account has 4 shared Picks.
consumerCostModel.comparison: Two 3-Pick promotions need 6 Picks, exceeding the 4-Pick pool by 2.

scenarios.scope: Illustrative framework; no consumer-specific transaction has been established

scenarios.name: Amazon Prime

consumerCostModel.headline: The subscription exit
consumerCostModel.constraint: FTC challenged consent and cancellation flow; settlement is not a finding about every signup.
consumerCostModel.comparison: Full cost = months subscribed × actual fee + any unwanted renewal months; unknown without account history.
consumerCostModel.formula: monthly fee × charged months + documented unwanted charges
